title: Dark Darker Darkest - Taking a Look
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lZj5qfUurLw

Daniel (@dungeondive) takes a look at Dark Darker Darkest and calls it, straightforwardly, Resident Evil 1 the board game — right down to survivor names like Bruce Romero and Nina Argento, and the same knot of tension he now finds hard to sit with in the video games.

The core loop is a lock-and-code hunt. Your survivors search a modular mansion for items whose icons combine into the code that opens the laboratory, where the antidote and a final confrontation with one of the Mortimers await. Meanwhile security cameras spot you and spawn worse things than zombies — guards, snakes, an undead gorilla — larger enemies carrying hit locations so damage actually means something. Fire spreads independently, destroying rooms permanently as it goes.

His honest warning is the rules. The Kickstarter shipped in a messy state and the original rulebook is, by reputation, unusable; he's playing from the designer's revised rules plus a cheat sheet, the FAQ and an icon guide. He suspects two survivors is too few, recommends four, and notes you can set the house up in a configuration that is genuinely unwinnable.

Not a game for him — but at ten dollars secondhand, an interesting one.

----

Dark Darker Darkest needs a revised rulebook, a cheat sheet and an FAQ before it plays well — at what point does a game's difficulty stop being the challenge and start being the documentation?
